prior_importants.description: The only thing that clears `conductor/blocked-since` is a look that sees the box `empty`. Any later non-empty look picks up the old timestamp, however long ago it was written. If no look happens while the box is empty, two separate short non-empty spells count as one long blockage. The conductor then shows up in Needs-you as `blocked` straight away, with a wrong age. This breaks the ADR's promise that "an operator typing into the conductor ... never shows up". A successful `tellConductor` also leaves the clock in place even though it sees an empty box at the end.

A refused tell can only come from the operator's `pup conductor tell`. Worker idle notices reach the conductor through Claude Code's peer socket (`notify_when_idle`) and never call `tellConductor`. So the clock still starts at the first `pup status` / `pup ui` look, and an operator who only runs `pup status` sees nothing on the first look after hours of blockage.

process_issues.description: The reviewer could not display the output of `gh pr diff 299`, which was too large. It reviewed only ADR 0168's format and its Amends/Amended-by handling, and did not check the changed src/ and test files against the convention docs.
The reviewer did not read ConductorBlocked, the DashboardNeed 'conductor' kind, or the isOperator mapping in src/cli/index.ts. It took them as plumbing the ADR prescribes.

The prior clock-merge important (conductor.service.ts 446-453) is resolved at head: noteConductorBox now stores the sight hash beside the time, and tellConductor notes its final look. The important about worker notices never calling tellConductor (comment at conductor.service.ts ~397-398, ADR 0168 ~line 42-49) is still unresolved and was not re-raised. The four prior nits were not addressed but were not re-raised either.
